title: People Pay More for a Box They Assembled Themselves
hook: People who built a box named a higher price for the same box

open.title: Same storage box, different price, and the only difference was who put it together
open.line: Two storage boxes are identical. One group built theirs and the other got theirs already assembled. Asked to set a price, the groups disagreed. Why?

summary: People paid more for IKEA boxes they built. The effect vanished if they took the build apart or never finished.

text: You've probably wrestled with flat-pack furniture.
Researchers gave university students IKEA storage boxes.
One group assembled theirs, and the other got boxes already assembled.
They asked what they'd pay for the box.
Those who built it offered $0.78 on average, and those who only received it offered $0.48.

panels.text: I worked hard on it, so it's worth more.

text: People valued their own creation at 23 cents and a stranger's clumsy one at 5 cents.
An expert's origami was valued at 27 cents.
So they rated their own clumsy work almost the same as an expert's.
The researchers called this the IKEA effect.
Actually, hard work alone wasn't enough.
When people built LEGO and then had to take it apart, the effect disappeared.
The same happened when people were stopped two steps before finishing a box.
Those who finished offered $1.46, and those who stopped offered $0.59.
